summary: The root حذر (Hdhr) conveys caution, wariness, and vigilance. It describes someone who is prepared, on guard, or fearful.
lane: حَذِرٌ ذ (S, A, Msb, K) and (S, A, K) Cautious; wary; vigilant; on his guard; careful; (S;) or in a state of preparation; (Msb;) as also ; (S, A, Msb;) and fearful: (S:) or very cautious or wary or vigilant or careful; as also (K) and : (A, K:) or this last signifies very fearful and cautious &c.: (S:) pl. of the first حَذِرُونَ and حَذَارَى . (S, K.) Sb cites, as an ex. of حَذِرٌ used transitively, حَذِرٌ أُمُورًا لَا تُخَافُ وَ آمِنٌ مَا لَيْسَ مُنْجِيهِ مِنَ الأَقْدَارِ [ Cautious, or very cautious, of things not to be feared, and trusting in that which will not save him from the decrees of destiny ]: but this is extr.; for an epithet of the measure فَعِلٌ is not [regularly] trans., so as to govern an objective complement. (S, TA.) In the Kur xxvi. 56, some read ; and some, حَذِرُونَ and : حاذرون signifying in a state of preparation; (Zj, S;) or fully equipped with arms: (Sh:) and حذرون , in a state of fear; (S;) or in a state of preparation; (TA;) or in a state of preparation with the accoutrements of war; (Ibn-Mes'ood;) or cautious, or vigilant. (Zj.)
